title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields, Part II: all CM fields
summary: Every elliptic curve over every CM number field is modular, with the parent's full local and archimedean conclusions. Layers 1-2 run the parent's geometric switch over an arbitrary CM field, proving the auxiliary curve modular over K before the cyclotomic base change when ζ5 ∉ K (Theorem 2.5). Layers 3-6 prove a potentially Barsotti-Tate lifting theorem at p = 5 over CM fields containing ζ5 with residual image SL₂(F5), by keeping a protected place with residually nontrivial unipotent inertia (Theorem 6.2). Layer 7 produces such a place on the auxiliary curve from a width-three degeneration, and Layer 8 proves the headline.

layers.title: Cyclotomic CM fields and descent of residual hypotheses

targets.name: isCMField_of_intermediate_cyclotomic
targets.statement: Let K be a CM number field and L/K a finite extension with IsCyclotomicExtension S K L. Every intermediate field K ⊆ E ⊆ L is a CM field; in particular L is CM.
hypotheses: K is a number field with NumberField.IsCMField K

locator.where: Proposition 1.4(b) with the uniqueness of complex conjugation noted after it, and Corollary 1.5, p. 10 (lines 273-295)

tests.name: cm_intermediate_Qzeta20
tests.statement: For K = Q(i), L = Q(zeta_20), the intermediate field Q(i, sqrt 5) is CM with maximal real subfield Q(sqrt 5).

tests.name: cm_intermediate_trivial
tests.statement: For S = {1, 2}, L = K and the statement is that K is CM.

tests.name: cm_intermediate_real_subfield
tests.statement: Q(sqrt 5) inside Q(zeta_20) is totally real and not CM: the statement needs E to contain K.

tests.name: cm_intermediate_abelian
tests.statement: For K = Q(sqrt -3), S = {4}, L = Q(zeta_12) and the conclusion agrees with NumberField.IsCMField.of_isAbelianGalois.

targets.name: decomposedGeneric_of_restrict
targets.statement: Let K ⊆ F be number fields with F/K finite and rbar : G_K → GL_n(k) continuous, k finite of characteristic ℓ. (a) A decomposed-generic prime for rbar|G_F is a decomposed-generic prime for rbar; hence rbar|G_F decomposed generic implies rbar decomposed generic. (b) If rbar|G_{F(ζ_ℓ)} is absolutely irreducible then so is rbar|G_{K(ζ_ℓ)}.
hypotheses: F/K finite extension of number fields

tests.name: generic_descent_trivial
tests.statement: For K = F = Q the statement is the identity.

tests.name: generic_no_ascent
tests.statement: 1 ⊕ 1 over F_3 is decomposed generic over Q with witness 2 but not over Q(zeta_3), where every completely split prime is 1 mod 3.

tests.name: generic_split_only_in_K
tests.statement: A prime split in K but not completely split in F is not a witness for rbar|G_F.

targets.name: K60_example
targets.statement: K60 = Q(ζ15 + ζ15⁻¹, i) is the fixed field of {1, 29} in (Z/60)ˣ; it is CM of degree 8, does not contain ζ5 (29 ≢ 1 mod 5), and K60(ζ3) = Q(ζ60) contains ζ5 (29 ≢ 1 mod 3). Hence ζ5 ∈ K60(μ_{3p}) for every p.

tests.name: K60_fixed_group
tests.statement: a ≡ ±1 mod 15 and a ≡ 1 mod 4 force a ∈ {1, 29} in (Z/60)ˣ.

layers.title: The switch over an arbitrary CM field

targets.name: cm_seed_before_base_change
targets.statement: With ζ5 ∉ K and t a switch parameter: (a) the mod-5 residual representation of H¹(A_t) is decomposed generic over K and absolutely irreducible on G_{K(ζ5)}, and A_t is geometrically non-CM; (b) A_t is modular over K by a cuspidal weight-zero π_A of PGL₂(𝔸_K) realizing H¹(A_t) at every (ℓ, ι); (c) F/K is finite abelian, F is CM, and the base change π_{A,F} is cuspidal weight zero with r_ι(π_{A,F}) ≅ V_η.
hypotheses: E/K is geometrically non-CM, y² = h(x)
p > max(100, 2[K:Q]+1) chosen as in the parent's §7.2 (general number-field form)
t ∈ U(K) produced by the parent's §7.4 simultaneous_specialization, in the §6.5 local_type_opens at every place above 3p

tests.name: seed_K60
tests.statement: Over K60, ζ5 ∉ K60 while ζ5 ∈ F: cm_modularity applies over K60 and not over F.

tests.name: seed_imag_quadratic
tests.statement: For imaginary quadratic K the parent's order (seed over F) gives the same π_{A,F} by strong multiplicity one.

tests.name: seed_cuspidality_needs_nonCM
tests.statement: A CM auxiliary curve could have non-cuspidal base change; §7.4(3) non-CM is needed.

targets.name: cm_switch_assembly
targets.statement: If one member of V_η is realized by a cuspidal weight-zero π_η of PGL₂(𝔸_F), then E is modular over K: H¹(E) is realized by a cuspidal weight-zero π_E of PGL₂(𝔸_K).
hypotheses: E/K is geometrically non-CM, y² = h(x)
p > max(100, 2[K:Q]+1) chosen as in the parent's §7.2 (general number-field form)
t ∈ U(K) produced by the parent's §7.4 simultaneous_specialization, in the §6.5 local_type_opens at every place above 3p
a cuspidal weight-zero π_η of PGL₂(𝔸_F) realizing one member of V_η

tests.name: assembly_lifting_primes
tests.statement: The lifting primes are 3, p, p with p > 100; the five-adic projective-field clause of potentiallySemistableCM never applies.

tests.name: assembly_square_twist
tests.statement: If h(t) is a square in K, χ_{h(t)} is trivial and π_E = π_B.

tests.name: assembly_quadratic_descent
tests.statement: At a quadratic descent step the two descents differ by the step's character; restriction alone does not choose; PAI §2.3(2) selects the one realizing H¹(B_t).

targets.name: cm_field_full_local_comparison
targets.statement: For K CM and E/K geometrically non-CM and modular: π_E is unique, has trivial central character, realizes H¹ at every (ℓ, ι); WD(H¹|G_{K_v})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(π_{E,v}) with N at every finite v ∤ ℓ; every finite local factor agrees; each complex place has parameter complexInfinityParameter; L(E/K, s) = L(π_E, s − 1/2).

tests.name: local_factor_degrees
tests.statement: Split multiplicative: degree 1 with N of rank 1; potentially good with nontrivial inertia: factor 1; good: degree 2.

tests.name: complex_parameter_i
tests.statement: At z = i the parameter is diag(i, −i): trace 0, determinant 1.

tests.name: unitary_shift
tests.statement: q = 4, a = 4: polynomial T² − 4T + 4, unitary roots 1, 1, fixing the shift s − 1/2.

targets.name: cm_field_cm_realization
targets.statement: For K CM and E/K geometrically CM by M: H¹(E)|G_{KM} is the sum of two algebraic Hecke-character realizations θ, θ'; if M ⊆ K, E is realized by θ ⊞ θ' over K (not cuspidal); if M ⊄ K, by AI_{KM/K}(θ), cuspidal; trivial central character, weight zero, all local parameters and L(E/K,s) = L(π_E, s − 1/2).
hypotheses: E/K geometrically CM by the imaginary quadratic field M

tests.name: cm_sum_case
tests.statement: Over Q(ζ8), y² = x³ − x has CM by Q(i) ⊆ K: isobaric sum.

tests.name: cm_induced_case
tests.statement: Over Q(ζ8), y² = x³ + 1 has CM by Q(√−3) ⊄ K: induction from Q(ζ24).

tests.name: cm_geometric
tests.statement: y² = x³ − x over Q(√−3) has no K-rational CM yet is geometrically CM and is induced.

targets.name: cm_modularity_zeta5_free
targets.statement: Let K be a CM field with ζ5 ∉ K. Every elliptic curve E/K is modular, with the conclusions of 2.3 (non-CM) or 2.4 (CM).

locator.where: Theorem 1.1, p. 2, line 86; proof §4.6 line 342; Lemma 5.1 line 357

tests.name: zeta5free_imag_quadratic
tests.statement: For imaginary quadratic K this is imaginary_quadratic_modularity.

tests.name: zeta5free_excludes_Qzeta5
tests.statement: Q(ζ5) contains ζ5 and is excluded; 8.1 covers it.

tests.name: zeta5free_K60
tests.statement: Over K60 the theorem applies although ζ5 ∈ K60(μ_{3p}).

layers.title: Finite-group and local cohomology at a protected place

targets.name: sl2AdjointRep
targets.statement: For a field k, sl2AdjointRep k is the representation of SL(2,k) on LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) k given by g·X = g X g⁻¹, built with Rep.ofDistribMulAction.

api.name: action_apply
api.statement: The action of g on X is the matrix product g X g⁻¹, k-linear and multiplicative in g; trace zero is preserved.

api.name: neg_one_acts_trivially
api.statement: The central element −1 acts trivially, so the representation factors through PSL₂(k).

api.name: trace_form_nondegenerate
api.statement: For odd characteristic the trace form tr(XY) is a nondegenerate invariant symmetric form identifying the representation with its dual.

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: For k → k' the base change of sl2AdjointRep k is the restriction of sl2AdjointRep k' along SL(2,k) → SL(2,k').

api.name: invariants_eq_bot
api.statement: For k of odd characteristic the SL(2,k)-invariants vanish.

tests.name: adjoint_U_action
tests.statement: For U = [[1,1],[0,1]]: e ↦ e, h ↦ h − 2e, f ↦ f + h − e; left multiplication would give Uf = f + E11 of trace 1.

tests.name: adjoint_scalar
tests.statement: 1 and −1 act as the identity; diag(2,3) over F5 scales e and f by 4 and fixes h.

tests.name: adjoint_char_two
tests.statement: In characteristic 2, ⟨h,h⟩ = 2 = 0 and the Gram determinant −2 vanishes: no self-duality.

tests.name: adjoint_unipotent_order
tests.statement: Over F5, (Ad U − 1)³ = 0 and (Ad U)⁵ = 1, while (Ad U − 1)² sends f to −2e ≠ 0.

targets.name: sl2Five_adjoint_restriction_unipotent_bijective
targets.statement: For U = [[1,1],[0,1]] in SL(2, F5), restriction H¹(SL(2,F5), ad⁰) → H¹(⟨U⟩, ad⁰), with ad⁰ the adjoint representation of 3.1, is bijective; both are one-dimensional and the target is spanned by the class of f. The same holds over any field k ⊇ F5 and for every subgroup of order five.

tests.name: res_F7_not_surjective
tests.statement: Over F7, H¹(SL(2,F7), ad⁰) = 0 while H¹ of the order-7 unipotent subgroup is one-dimensional: bijectivity is special to 5.

tests.name: res_F3_zero
tests.statement: Over F3 the norm of Ad U is (D−1)² ≠ 0 and H¹(⟨U⟩, ad⁰) = 0.

tests.name: res_order_three
tests.statement: Restriction to the order-3 subgroup generated by [[0,−1],[1,−1]] is zero on H¹ since 3 is invertible in F5.

targets.name: IsProtected
targets.statement: For p odd, F_v finite over Q_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p, k finite of characteristic p and ρbar : G_{F_v} → GL₂(k) continuous, ρbar is protected if ρbar(I_v) is nontrivial and consists of unipotent matrices.

api.name: factors_tame
api.statement: ρbar|I_v factors through the coefficient-p tame quotient; ρbar(I_v) is cyclic of order p generated by ρbar(τ), equal to U in a suitable basis.

api.name: frobenius_upper_triangular
api.statement: In that basis ρbar(φ) is upper triangular with diagonal ratio q_v; if q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρbar(φ) = a(1 + bE12), and for b ∈ F_p a change of tame lift makes it scalar.

api.name: restrict_prime_to_p
api.statement: Preserved by restriction to extensions of ramification index prime to p, by unramified twists and by duality; destroyed when p divides the ramification index.

tests.name: protected_tate
tests.statement: A split Tate curve with p ∤ v(q) has E_q[p] protected, inertia acting by [[1, v(q)t_p],[0,1]].

tests.name: protected_tate_divisible
tests.statement: If p | v(q), E_q[p] is unramified and not protected (q = ϖ⁵, p = 5).

tests.name: protected_semisimple_inertia
tests.statement: Over F5 with q_v = 11, an order-three tame inertia quotient with generator ↦ M = [[0,−1],[1,−1]] and Frobenius ↦ Φ = [[4,1],[0,1]]: M³ = 1, ΦMΦ⁻¹ = [[4,1],[4,0]] = M⁻¹ = M¹¹, char poly X² + X + 1; inertia nontrivial and not unipotent, so not protected. diag(ζ3, ζ3⁻¹) needs F25 since #F5ˣ = 4.

tests.name: protected_lost_index_p
tests.statement: After ramification index 5, residual inertia becomes U⁵ = 1.

targets.name: protected_unipotent_inertia_smooth
targets.statement: For ρbar protected, ψ unramified lifting det ρbar and ρ_A a lift to A ∈ CNL_O with det ψ, TFAE: (i) every σ ∈ I_v has char poly (X−1)²; (ii) (ρ_A(τ) − 1)² = 0; (iii) ρ_A is minimally ramified. These lifts form a deformation problem with framed fixed-determinant ring O[[x1,x2,x3]], and every lift satisfies q_v (tr ρ_A(φ))² = (1 + q_v)² ψ(φ).
hypotheses: ψ unramified with ψ mod 𝔪 = det ρbar

tests.name: uni_nonunipotent_lift
tests.statement: ρ(τ) = [[ζ5, 1],[0, ζ5⁻¹]] reduces to U but has char poly (X−ζ5)(X−ζ5⁻¹).

tests.name: uni_first_order
tests.statement: (1+εf)U has trace 2+ε and fails (i); (1+εh)U has trace 2, determinant 1 and satisfies it.

tests.name: uni_residual_frobenius_entry
tests.statement: k = F25, q_v = 11, ρbar(τ) = U, ρbar(φ) = 1 + ζE12 with ζ ∉ F5: protected, residual upper-right entry z̄ = ζ ≠ 0, not removable by φ ↦ φτ^x (ζ ↦ ζ + x, x ∈ F5); the third coordinate is z − [ζ], and z is a unit on every lift.

targets.name: protected_tangent_self_annihilating
targets.statement: For ρbar protected and M = ad⁰ρbar: (a) L_v = H¹_ur(F_v, M), of dimension h⁰(F_v, M) (1 if q_v ≡ 1 mod p, else 0); (b) L_v^⊥ = H¹_ur(F_v, M(1)); (c) if μ_p ⊂ F_v, h⁰ = h² = 1, h¹ = 2 and L_v is its own annihilator under M(1) ≅ M; (d) for p ≥ 5, ρbar(τ) = U, ρbar(φ) = 1: H¹ = k[(f,0)] ⊕ k[(0,e)] and L_v = k[(0,e)].

tests.name: tangent_dims_mu5
tests.statement: With μ5 ⊂ F_v: M^{I} = ke, h⁰ = h² = 1, h¹ = 2.

tests.name: tangent_no_mu5
tests.statement: For q_v ≡ 2 mod 5, φ scales e by 2: h⁰ = 0 and L_v = 0.

tests.name: tangent_cocycles
tests.statement: Cocycles (c(τ), c(φ)) with c(φ) ∈ ke: dim Z¹ = 4, dim B¹ = 2, dim H¹ = 2.

tests.name: tangent_ramified_class
tests.statement: (f,0) is not in L_v and pairs nontrivially with (0,e).

layers.title: Global Galois cohomology at five with a protected place

targets.name: exceptional_classes_ramify
targets.statement: F a number field with μ5 ⊂ F, ρbar : G_F → GL₂(k) with image conjugate to SL₂(F5), M = ad⁰ρbar, L = field cut out by ρbar, C_N = F(μ_{5^N}), v ∤ 5 protected. A class κ ∈ H¹(G_F, M) vanishing on G_{LC_N} and unramified at v is zero; restriction to G_{LC_N} is injective on classes of H¹(G_{F,S}, M(1)) satisfying L_v^⊥ at v.
hypotheses: image of ρbar conjugate to SL₂(F5)

tests.name: exceptional_without_protection
tests.statement: With no protected place, the inflated exceptional class dies on G_L and is unramified wherever ρbar is.

tests.name: exceptional_order_two_inertia
tests.statement: Inertia image of order 2 kills every class of H¹(SL₂(F5), ad⁰).

tests.name: exceptional_F7
tests.statement: For image SL₂(F7), H¹(SL₂(F7), ad⁰) = 0 and no protection is needed.

targets.name: protected_taylor_wiles_primes
targets.statement: With S = T ⊔ P (T ⊇ places above 5, P nonempty protected), H_Q the dual group with conditions L_v^⊥ at P and 0 at Q: for every N ≥ 1, r ≥ dim H_∅ and finite B, there is a level-N Taylor-Wiles datum Q_N of exactly r degree-one places outside S ∪ B with H_{Q_N} = 0; their rational primes are unramified in F and split in every imaginary quadratic subfield.

tests.name: tw_diag23
tests.statement: diag(2,3) ∈ SL₂(F5), distinct eigenvalues, Ad scales e,f by 4 and fixes h: one-dimensional coinvariants.

tests.name: tw_framed_P_fails
tests.statement: Framing a protected place drops its dual condition; the inflated exceptional class is locally trivial at every Taylor-Wiles prime and survives.

tests.name: tw_padding
tests.statement: For H_∅ = 0 the padding class still gives exactly r primes.

targets.name: protected_relative_presentation
targets.statement: F CM with μ5 ⊂ F, d = [F⁺:Q], S = T ⊔ P with t = |T|, problem 𝒮 with conditions R_v at T and unipotent inertia at P, Q_N from 4.2 with |Q_N| = r: R^{□T}_{𝒮_{Q_N}} is a quotient of R^loc_T[[x_1..x_g]] with g = r − 3d − 1 + t, R^loc_T = ⊗_{v∈T} R_v.

tests.name: presentation_d1
tests.statement: d = 1, t = 1, r = 3 gives g = 0, as in CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §9.3.

tests.name: presentation_dims
tests.statement: d = 2, t = 3, r = 10: dim R^loc = 14, g = 6, dim R_∞ = 20 = r + 4t − d, dim S_∞ = 22: deficit 2 = d.

tests.name: presentation_framed_P
tests.statement: Framing P keeps the deficit d but loses the dual condition of 4.2.

layers.title: Hecke algebras and patching with a protected place

targets.name: ProtectedPreparedDatum
targets.statement: A CM field F ∋ μ5, ι, S = S5 ⊔ R ⊔ P (S5 = S5^cr ⊔ S5^st, R ∪ P prime to 5, P ≠ ∅, P^c ∩ S = ∅) and cuspidal weight-zero π of PGL₂(𝔸_F) with: (i) imaginary quadratic splitting of primes below S or ramified in F; (ii) five-adic degree condition and residue fields > F5; (iii) π unramified outside R ∪ P ∪ S5^st, Iwahori-fixed vectors there; (iv) ι-ordinary non-crystalline ordinary at S5^st; (v) ρbar = rbar_ι(π) with image SL₂(F5), decomposed generic; (vi) ρbar trivial at S5 ∪ R; (vii) ρbar protected at P.

api.name: level
api.statement: K^P = ∏ K_v with PGL₂(O_v) outside R ∪ P ∪ S5^st and Iw_v on R ∪ P ∪ S5^st; no pro-v Iwahori places.

api.name: framingSet
api.statement: T = S5 ⊔ R; parabolics at five and the maximal ideal as in CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §9.4.

api.name: perfect
api.statement: Localized complexes at K^P are perfect by CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §8.7 (ζ5 ∈ F, absolutely irreducible ρbar, coefficients trivial mod ϖ).

api.name: toCNData
api.statement: Forgetting P into the Iwahori places gives CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §9.1 data (1)-(14) except (14) at P, with ζ5 ∈ F and S = S5 ∪ R ∪ P; clause (15) fails.

tests.name: datum_P_empty
tests.statement: P = ∅ is excluded: it is the configuration removed by clause (15).

tests.name: datum_conjugate_in_R
tests.statement: v ∈ P with v^c ∈ R violates P^c ∩ S = ∅.

tests.name: datum_degree_condition
tests.statement: [F⁺:Q] = 8 with five-adic local degrees (1,1,6): condition (ii) fails at the degree-6 place (complementary sums 1); with eight places of degree 1 it holds (sum 6 > 4).

tests.name: datum_residue_F5
tests.statement: A residue field F5 above five violates (ii).

targets.name: protectedDeformationProblem
targets.statement: For a protected prepared datum, χ = (χ_v)_{v∈R} trivial mod ϖ and a Taylor-Wiles datum Q: 𝒮^P_χ is CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §9.5's 𝒮_χ on S5 ∪ R plus the unipotent-inertia condition of 3.4 at P, framed at T = S5 ⊔ R; 𝒮^P_{χ,Q} adds unrestricted fixed-determinant rings at Q with the O[Δ_Q]-structure.

api.name: reduction
api.statement: 𝒮^P_χ and 𝒮^P_1 agree modulo ϖ.

api.name: augmentation
api.statement: Killing the augmentation ideal of O[Δ_Q] recovers 𝒮^P_χ.

api.name: presentation
api.statement: The T-framed rings have the presentation of 4.3 over R^loc_χ of dimension 1 + 3t + 2d.

api.name: coefficients
api.statement: The coefficient module on K^P is O(χ⁻¹) at R and trivial at P.

tests.name: problem_Q_empty
tests.statement: Q = ∅ gives 𝒮^P_χ; χ = 1 gives trivial coefficients.

tests.name: problem_not_LGDR_steinberg
tests.statement: LocalGaloisDeformationRings §2.5's Steinberg lifts need trivial residual data and do not apply at P.

tests.name: problem_local_dim
tests.statement: d = 1, one five-adic place of degree 2, R = ∅: dim R^loc_χ = 6; P adds nothing.

targets.name: protected_hecke_condition
targets.statement: There are N depending only on [F:Q], ideals J_{χ,Q} with J^N = 0 and surjective O[Δ_Q]-algebra maps R_{𝒮^P_{χ,Q}} → T_{χ,Q}/J_{χ,Q} matching Frobenius characteristic polynomials outside S ∪ Q and compatible with reduction (χ to 1) and augmentation (Q to ∅).

tests.name: hecke_torus_poly
tests.statement: At full Iwahori level with trivial character the torus polynomial at P is (X−1)²; with character χ_v it would be (X−χ_v(u))(X−χ_v(u)⁻¹).

tests.name: hecke_pro_v_level
tests.statement: At pro-v Iwahori level the torus operators act through k_vˣ and (X−1)² is not forced.

tests.name: hecke_Q_empty
tests.statement: For Q = ∅, Δ_∅ = 1 and the maps are the first construction.

targets.name: protected_prepared_lifting
targets.statement: For a protected prepared datum and ρ : G_F → GL₂(Q̄5) continuous with ρbar ≅ rbar_ι(π), det ε5⁻¹, unramified outside S, unipotent inertia at R ∪ P, Barsotti-Tate at S5^cr with matching ordinarity, non-crystalline extension of ε5⁻¹ by 1 at S5^st: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal weight-zero Π of PGL₂(𝔸_F).

locator.where: Theorem 4.2 and proof, lines 410-498; CN23 Prop 5.6.1 line 4261

tests.name: lifting_nonunipotent_target
tests.statement: A target with inertia at P through ζ5^{±1} is not a point of the patched problem.

tests.name: lifting_matching_components
tests.statement: A supersingular target with an ordinary source is excluded at S5^cr.

tests.name: lifting_deficit
tests.statement: d = 1: deficit 1 = l₀ for PGL₂ over an imaginary quadratic field.

targets.name: protected_solvable_preparation
targets.statement: F CM with ζ5 ∈ F, ρ, π satisfying CN23 Theorem 5.2 (1)-(3),(5) at p = 5 with ρbar(G_F) ≅ SL₂(F5), P nonempty with: ρbar protected, ρ(I_v) unipotent, π_v^{Iw} ≠ 0, ρ and π unramified at v^c. There is a finite solvable Galois CM F'/F, disjoint from the field of ρbar, with P ∪ P^c split completely, such that the base-changed data satisfy 5.1 and the hypotheses of 5.4.

locator.where: end of proof of Theorem 5.2, lines 4433-4509; CaptainSude26 proof of Prop. 5.2 lines 543-603

tests.name: prep_index_five
tests.statement: A completion of ramification index 5 above P makes residual inertia U⁵ = 1.

tests.name: prep_conjugate_ramified
tests.statement: If v and v^c are both ramified, completions above v and v^c are isomorphic in every CM extension and P'^c ∩ S' = ∅ cannot be reached.

tests.name: prep_Qzeta5
tests.statement: F = Q(ζ5) has no imaginary quadratic subfield; the imaginary quadratic composita are needed for (i) of 5.1.

targets.name: steinberg_protected_lifting
targets.statement: F CM, ρ : G_F → GL₂(Q̄5) satisfying CN23 Theorem 5.2 (1),(2),(3),(5) at p = 5. If either (4) holds or there is a nonempty finite set P of places v ∤ 5 with ρbar(I_v) nontrivial unipotent, ρ(I_v) unipotent, π_v^{Iw} ≠ 0, and ρ, π unramified at v^c, then ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal regular algebraic weight-zero Π of PGL₂(𝔸_F).

locator.where: §4 and Theorem 4.2, lines 264-498; CN23 Theorem 5.2 lines 3849-3872, Lemma 6.1.4 line 4562

tests.name: lifting_det_order_two
tests.statement: ζ5 ∉ F, det of order 2: an element of determinant −1 times 2 has determinant (−1)·4 = 1, the projective images agree and (4) holds.

tests.name: lifting_imag_quadratic
tests.statement: For imaginary quadratic F, ζ5 ∉ F and the theorem is potentiallySemistableCM.

tests.name: lifting_tate_divisible
tests.statement: A split Tate place with 5 | v(Δ) has unramified residual representation and is not protected.

targets.name: width_three_degeneration
targets.statement: For R_* of exact order 2n with [n]R_* = a/2: (a) the image of (O,1) is a k-point of D_t, so D_t ≅ A_t; (b) w fixes exactly one of the three nodes of the m = 3 nodal model, acting by −1 on both branches, and exchanges the other two; (c) the quotient has an A1 point uv = s² and a node of thickness one, and after resolution is a cycle of three rational curves (type I3); (d) 1/j(A_t) has a zero of order 3 in s and the Tate parameter is c s³ h(s), c ≠ 0, h(0) = 1.

tests.name: width_genus_check
tests.statement: Three fixed nodes would give two rational curves meeting in three points, arithmetic genus 2, contradicting genus 1.

tests.name: width_thickness
tests.statement: Total thickness 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = 2 + 1: type I3, not I2.

tests.name: width_p101
tests.statement: p = 101: R_* has order 606, [303]R_* = a/2, x unramified at R_*.

targets.name: auxiliary_prime_opens
targets.statement: There is a finite set Σ0 of rational primes such that for q ∉ Σ0, q ≥ 7, q ≠ p, split completely in the field of the data of 7.1(b) and in the normal closure of K, and each place v | q: (a) a nonempty open Ω_v ⊂ U(K_v) on which A_t is split multiplicative with v(Δ_min) = 3k_v, 5 ∤ k_v; (b) for every other v' | q a nonempty open on which A_t has good reduction.

tests.name: opens_k5
tests.statement: v(s) = 5 gives v(Δ_min) = 15, residual inertia trivial, not protected; v(s) = 1 or 7 give 3 or 21.

tests.name: opens_all_places
tests.statement: Constraining only v would leave v^c possibly bad, violating 6.2's condition at v^c.

tests.name: opens_q5
tests.statement: q = 5 is excluded: the place would not be prime to the coefficient prime.

targets.name: tate_curve_protected
targets.statement: For K_v finite over Q_ℓ, ℓ ≠ 5, μ5 ⊂ K_v and A/K_v split multiplicative with 5 ∤ v(Δ_min): A[5] and the residual H¹ are protected, residual Frobenius has diagonal 1 and becomes trivial after a tame-lift change, inertia acts unipotently on H¹(A, Q̄5), and for modular non-CM A the local component is Steinberg. If 5 | v(Δ_min), A[5] is unramified.

tests.name: tate_v3
tests.statement: v(q) = 3: residual inertia [[1,3],[0,1]]; v(q) = 15: trivial.

tests.name: tate_nonsplit
tests.statement: Non-split multiplicative: residual Frobenius diagonal −1, still protected, component the unramified quadratic twist of Steinberg.

tests.name: tate_good
tests.statement: Good reduction gives unramified A[5], never protected.

targets.name: switch_five_retained_places
targets.statement: F CM, ρbar : G_F → GL₂(F5) with det ε̄5 decomposed generic, partition of the five-adic places, F_avoid, a finite set Σ of places not above 2,3,5 and nonempty opens Ω_w ⊂ Y_ρbar(F_w). There are L/F finite solvable Galois CM, L ∩ F_avoid = F, Σ split completely, and non-CM modular A'/L with A'[5] ≅ ρbar|G_L, the prescribed reduction above five, ρbar|G_L decomposed generic, and A' in Ω_w at every place above w ∈ Σ.
hypotheses: ρbar decomposed generic with det ε̄5

locator.where: Proposition 5.2 and proof, lines 538-603; CN23 Prop. 6.1.5 line 4574; CHT08 Lemma 4.1.2

tests.name: switch_sigma_empty
tests.statement: Σ = ∅ gives switch_five.

tests.name: switch_sigma_two
tests.statement: A place of Σ above 2 would conflict with the mandatory Tate condition.

tests.name: switch_split_needed
tests.statement: An unramified quadratic completion at w ∈ Σ changes F_w and the meaning of Ω_w.

targets.name: protected_auxiliary_seed
targets.statement: K CM with μ5 ⊂ K, E/K geometrically non-CM, p from the parent's §7.2, q, v from 7.2 (q prime to bad reduction of E). There is a switch parameter t also in the 7.2 opens; for every such t: (a) A_t[5] has image SL₂(F5) over K and is decomposed generic; (b) H¹(A_t) is protected at v and unramified at v^c; (c) A_t is modular over K.

tests.name: seed_transvections_generate
tests.statement: [[1,3],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[3,1]] generate a subgroup of order 120 of SL₂(F5); one transvection gives order 5.

tests.name: seed_det_trivial
tests.statement: Over Q(ζ5), det A_t[5] = ε̄5 is trivial on G_K, so the image is SL₂(F5).

tests.name: seed_nonCM
tests.statement: A CM curve has an abelian subgroup of index ≤ 2 in its image; SL₂(F5) is perfect of order 120.

layers.title: Every elliptic curve over every CM field

targets.name: cm_field_modularity
targets.statement: For every CM number field K and every elliptic curve E/K there is an isobaric weight-zero π_E of GL₂(𝔸_K) with trivial central character realizing H¹(E) at every (ℓ, ι), with full WD compatibility at every finite v ∤ ℓ, agreement of all finite local factors, complexInfinityParameter at every complex place and L(E/K,s) = L(π_E, s − 1/2); cuspidal if E is geometrically non-CM, induction or isobaric sum otherwise.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1, line 26, proof line 671; LeHung26 Remark 1.3.1 line 125

tests.name: headline_Qzeta5
tests.statement: K = Q(ζ5): only the ζ5 ∈ K branch applies; its quadratic subfield Q(√5) is real.

tests.name: headline_K60_two_routes
tests.statement: Over K60 both branches (directly, or over Q(ζ60) with descent) give the same π_E by strong multiplicity one.

tests.name: headline_imag_quadratic
tests.statement: For imaginary quadratic K this is imaginary_quadratic_modularity.

tests.name: headline_biquadratic
tests.statement: Q(√−1, √5) does not contain ζ5 (Galois group (Z/2)² versus cyclic of order 4) and is covered by 2.5.

gaps.title: Torsion inertial comparison at Iwahori places (ACC Theorem 3.1.1)
gaps.detail: Theorem 5.3 needs ACC Theorem 3.1.1 for GL_2 in the setting of ACC23 §3.1: F CM containing an imaginary quadratic field with every p-adic place of F⁺ split in F; a good level; a finite conjugation-stable S containing the p-adic places with ACC's conditions outside S; R ⊆ S prime to p with residue characteristics split in imaginary quadratic subfields, Iw_{v,1} ⊆ K_v ⊆ Iw_v on R and K_v hyperspecial on R^c ∖ R; a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Conclusion: N depending only on the rank and [F:Q], an ideal I_R with I_R^N = 0 in the Hecke algebra with torus operators at R, and a representation of G_{F,S∖(R^c∖R)} over the quotient with Hecke Frobenius polynomials and characteristic polynomial P_{v,σ} at every σ ∈ W_{F_v}, v ∈ R. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure and CrystallineLocalGlobalCompatibilityCM §9.7 (and §9.9 through it) cite this as AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5, whose text states characteristic-zero comparisons only.
